news.text: 7 November saw the launch of the **Mars Global Surveyor** from Cape Canaveral in Florida. The probe was sent to map the planet's surface features and work out what its rocks and soil are made of. It was due to circle Mars roughly every two hours at about 235 miles up, helping scientists pick landing sites for future rover missions, and it kept working for almost ten years before contact was lost.

12 November saw the debut of the music-themed comedy panel show *Never Mind The Buzzcocks* on the BBC. Hosted by **Mark Lamarr**, with team captains **Phil Jupitus** and **Sean Hughes**, it quickly became must-watch television thanks to its sarcastic humour and habit of taunting its guests.

news.text: 18 November saw the worldwide premiere of the film *Star Trek: First Contact*. A Borg escape pod heads for Earth after the Borg cube is destroyed by a fleet led by **Picard**, and the new **USS Enterprise** follows it through a time distortion into the 21st century. To stop Earth being assimilated, the crew must help **Zefram Cochrane** build the first faster-than-light spacecraft.

26 November saw the death of comedian, actor and writer **Michael Bentine** from prostate cancer, aged 74. He was best remembered as a founding member of *The Goons*, the radio comedy show that ran from 1951 to 1960.

gaming.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert
gaming.reviewQuote: Albert Einstein, Soviet Mammoth Tanks, and Hell March. Westwood has delivered the definitive PC strategy experience.
gaming.headline: Time Travel, Mammoth Tanks, and the Thumping Hell March
gaming.gameplay: Developed by Westwood Studios in Las Vegas, *Command & Conquer: Red Alert* plunged players into an alternate timeline where Albert Einstein used a chrono-displacement device to assassinate Adolf Hitler in 1924, inadvertently unleashing an unchecked Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin to invade Western Europe. Players chose between the technologically cunning **Allies** (Chronospheres, GPS satellites, Tanya Adams) and the brute mechanized strength of the **Soviets** (Mammoth Tanks, Tesla Coils, Iron Curtain invulnerability).
gaming.reception: Releasing in November 1996, *Red Alert* became an astronomical commercial smash on PC, shifting over 1.5 million copies in its first month alone. Critics praised its campy live-action FMV cutscenes starring Frank Klepacki's legendary industrial metal track **"Hell March"**, while local LAN and modem multiplayer turned dorm rooms and offices into late-night tank-rush warzones.
gaming.impact: *Red Alert* cemented Westwood Studios alongside Blizzard as the twin rulers of the real-time strategy golden age. Its fast-paced base building, instant unit queues, and irresistible alternate-history swagger established it as one of the most beloved PC strategy games of all time.
